features.text: The patient has been experiencing numbness and tingling in both hands for a few weeks.
The numbness and tingling started after a car wreck last December when the patient broke both wrists.
The symptoms have worsened over the last month.
The numbness and tingling sometimes radiate up the arms.
The patient has been wearing splints on both wrists, with the right one being worse.
The patient was given nerve pain medicine but hasn't been taking it as prescribed.
The patient has not undergone any neurological evaluations or imaging studies like an MRI or EMG.
The patient has not been scheduled for the nerve test yet.
The patient experiences hand weakness, especially when using them.
The patient has difficulty gripping things and performing daily tasks like buttoning shirts or turning doorknobs.
The patient experiences soreness and a throbbing feeling in the hands.
The patient has not been evaluated by a neurologist or orthopedic specialist for these symptoms.
The patient has not been scheduled for imaging studies of the wrists or hands since the car wreck.
The patient has not undergone any nerve conduction studies or EMG tests.
The patient has not been evaluated for cervical spine issues.
The patient has not had any cervical spine imaging like X-rays or MRI.
The patient experiences worsening of numbness and tingling at night.
The patient experiences changes in grip strength and difficulty with tasks requiring hand coordination, such as writing or using tools.
